name: setup
description: Can an agent get Astryx into an app that already has Tailwind, without damaging the app? The design system is installed in NO condition — installing it is the task. The only variable is the guidance surface the agent can find; the outcome is the rendered app, measured against itself before the install.

base.notes: Existing Tailwind v4 console: `@import 'tailwindcss'`, its own `:root` vocabulary and `@theme inline` mapping (--color-card, --color-border, --color-accent, --radius-md), real shadcn components under components/ui, house conventions in README.md + AGENTS.md, a dark surface that is CSS variables rather than a color-mode system. It builds and renders before every run.

conditions.label: Public docs only (floor)
conditions.hypothesis: The agent finds the package README and `astryx docs styling-libraries`, and both print a Tailwind recipe written for an empty globals.css. Applied to a file that already has content, it builds clean and repaints the app. Expect silent-damage, not a failed build.

conditions.label: AGENTS.md points at the CLI
conditions.hypothesis: Discovery improves — more doc lookups before the first edit — but the recipe the agent then finds is the same greenfield one, so the damage is unchanged. If this arm moves the score, the problem was discovery; if it doesn't, the problem is the recipe.

conditions.label: An existing-app recipe exists
conditions.hypothesis: The candidate guidance: keep the app's Tailwind entry, declare the layer order ABOVE it, skip the bridge unless the app wants its vocabulary re-pointed, tell the provider the app's color scheme, and re-assert any colliding app token on the theme boundary. This is the arm that decides whether a doc change is worth shipping.

conditions.label: Handed the exact edits (ceiling)
conditions.hypothesis: Damage is near zero by construction. What this arm measures is the RESIDUE — what an install costs an existing app even when nobody makes a mistake. Residue the ceiling cannot remove is a product finding, filed against the packages, not a guidance gap.

measurement.reference: The pristine app, measured by the same code before the agent starts.
measurement.notes: Both color schemes are measured in every run. The system paints through light-dark() and the fixture has no color-mode system for it to read, so an arm can be correct on a dark-mode laptop and unreadable in headless CI. A single-scheme test would inherit whichever machine ran it.
measurement.emitted_css: The cascade is read off the built bundle, never the source. The `@layer` statement does not survive compilation — Tailwind rewrites it and the bundle carries only `@layer components;` — so the effective order is the order the layer BLOCKS first appear in the output. An arm can carry a correct-looking statement and ship the inverse cascade.
